questions.note: Judged fresh on the round-6 captures. ATTRIBUTED -- RESOLVED. Both claim rows now open with the organisation's own name, whole and linked, at the cell's left edge, and the ellipsis lands on the quoted words instead: Google DeepMind's row and Tencent's row each name their attributing party before anything is elided. The defect F-sys-5-1 measured -- one name cut mid-word and dateless, one name absent behind the clamp -- is gone, and gone structurally: whatever renders first is the last thing the line box can lose, so the attribution cannot be truncated by a longer claim. Identical in light and dark at the widest capture. LABELLED: unchanged and still first-viewport in all four captures -- the lede states in words that vendor claims are quoted verbatim from the vendor, are not verified by this site, and that a blank means no claim on file, with a derived count that agrees with the board in both themes. BLANKS: every claimless row still reads its absence in words, italic and muted over hatch. THIRD-PARTY: nothing measured renders as vendor speech; the round narrowed admission further (registrable-domain matching replacing the label scan) and the rendered set is unchanged, so no new value entered the column. At the narrow capture the column is off-frame exactly as at v5 and the lede remains the reader's whole contact with it -- unchanged, not a regression. Residual, not re-filed: with the source first the value is now what the clamp eats, so at a glance one cell shows the vendor plus a bare leading digit. That is uninformative, never dishonest -- the truncation is visibly a truncation and the row still names who is speaking -- and the clamp is do_not_touch as a form, so it is recorded in downstream rather than as a defect on a final round.

carried_forward.note: Invariant met: for every row rendering a vendor claim the attributing party's name is legible untruncated in the cell, in both themes, at the widest captured viewport. The implementer took the ordering half of the prescription and left the clamp alone, which is the form the finding asked for. No successor filed.

diagnosis.strongest: ALLR: the column finally says all three things at once -- who is speaking, that nobody here checked them, and where the silences are. The admission rule matches the label, and now the label's subject is named in the row rather than deleted by the layout.
diagnosis.weakest: The board's honesty is carried almost entirely by one sentence of lede plus a two-row column; the structure that proves the sentence is still mostly absence.
diagnosis.critical_issue: None. q8 holds PASS and the one residual open against the anchor is closed.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Nothing further inside this directive's fence. The next real gain is giving the claim cell room to show a quoted fragment worth reading, which is a form change and out of scope for a final micro-fix.

downstream.weakness: Vendor-first ordering makes the source unelidable by making the claim elidable, so the column's informational half now degrades silently as claims get longer -- Tencent's cell already shows only its opening figures. The board reads honest and says little.
downstream.cause: A one-line clamp holds two things that both want the line: an attribution that must survive whole and a quotation that only means something whole. Ordering picks a winner; it does not create room.
downstream.recommendation: Keep the ordering as the permanent rule. When the fence next opens, give the claim its own line beneath the name rather than widening the column, so the fix holds at the narrow viewport too -- where the column is off-frame and the lede is doing all the work.
